topic.title: Work: A woman teaches sewing in a refugee camp
topic.focus: A woman teaches sewing in a refugee camp

candidate_instructions: Read all five sections. Answer Questions 1-5. Follow the stated word limits exactly.

sections.heading: A camp far from home
sections.text: In 2017, there is a refugee camp in Uganda. 5,000 people live here. They escaped from their country. They have nothing. A woman named Amira is 45 years old. She is good at sewing.

sections.heading: Sewing class begins
sections.text: Amira starts a sewing class in her tent. Young women come to learn. She teaches them to sew clothes. She teaches them to fix clothes. The class is free. Amira does it with her heart.

sections.heading: Making clothes to sell
sections.text: After two months, the women make beautiful dresses and scarves. They sell them to people outside the camp. They earn good money. The money helps feed their families. The women are proud of their work. They have dignity.

sections.heading: More than sewing
sections.text: The sewing class becomes very popular. Now 60 women come every week. Amira teaches them sewing, but also life skills. She teaches them to be strong. She teaches them to hope. The tent becomes a happy place.

sections.heading: A future beyond the camp
sections.text: Today, some women have opened their own small shops. They make and sell clothes. They earn enough money to rent a house outside the camp. They leave the camp with hope and a job. Amira says needle and thread can give back freedom.

passage.full_text:
Paragraph 1 — A camp far from home
In 2017, there is a refugee camp in Uganda. 5,000 people live here. They escaped from their country. They have nothing. A woman named Amira is 45 years old. She is good at sewing.

Paragraph 2 — Sewing class begins
Amira starts a sewing class in her tent. Young women come to learn. She teaches them to sew clothes. She teaches them to fix clothes. The class is free. Amira does it with her heart.

Paragraph 3 — Making clothes to sell
After two months, the women make beautiful dresses and scarves. They sell them to people outside the camp. They earn good money. The money helps feed their families. The women are proud of their work. They have dignity.

Paragraph 4 — More than sewing
The sewing class becomes very popular. Now 60 women come every week. Amira teaches them sewing, but also life skills. She teaches them to be strong. She teaches them to hope. The tent becomes a happy place.

Paragraph 5 — A future beyond the camp
Today, some women have opened their own small shops. They make and sell clothes. They earn enough money to rent a house outside the camp. They leave the camp with hope and a job. Amira says needle and thread can give back freedom.
